definition: Nonfluent aphasia, as supported here, refers to primary progressive nonfluent aphasia, a clinical syndrome within frontotemporal lobar degeneration. It is part of a neurodegenerative condition involving frontal and temporal lobe atrophy and is associated with progressive changes in language function.

provenance.scope: Source record D057174; pinned source text

The definition narrows the term to a specific subtype without support from the packet’s wording; the source only states that FTLD includes primary progressive nonfluent aphasia among its syndromes.
